Mark — thanks for the file and the clear ask. High level answers first, then proposed next steps.

Short answers:
- Server-side telemetry: by default Redwood collects request-level metadata (timestamps, model id, route, token counts) and an account-scoped request id. We do not persist third-party advertising cookies or platform-specific advertising IDs in the standard telemetry unless you opt into forwarding them.
- Cookie syncing: when you enable server-side collection we offer two modes: 
  1) Passthrough: Redwood forwards raw cookie headers to downstream partners exactly as received (not recommended for ad identifiers unless you control partner contracts).
  2) Tokenized mapping: Redwood can map client cookies to a hashed token (deterministic salted hash per-account) that you control. That token is what appears in logs and can be shared with ad partners without exposing raw identifiers.
- DPA/subprocessors: telemetry storage and ingestion use our hosted telemetry pipeline in US regions by default; subprocessors involved typically include our cloud provider, a managed logging vendor, and a secrets/KMS provider. We can provide a tailored subprocessor list and an exportable data flow diagram for your legal team.

Next steps I propose:
- Neha (legal) will outline recommended DPA language and confirm whether the tokenized mapping meets Helix's transfer requirements.
- I'll attach a short design doc that shows the two modes and the default data retention periods. Could you confirm whether Helix requires advertising IDs to be retained for measurement? That will determine if we need additional contractual safeguards.

Putting the initial design doc here — redwood-server-telemetry-design.pdf (attached). Happy to hop on a 30-min screen share this week.

Best,
Marcus Lin

Hi Mark / Marcus — Neha from Legal. Quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Tokenization approach: if Helix chooses the deterministic salted-hash token, that token is generated using a salt unique to Helix and stored only within your account scope. From a DPA viewpoint, the token is pseudonymized data. We can add explicit DPA language that prohibits un-salting by Redwood and limits disclosure to named subprocessors.

2) Transfers: our default telemetry pipeline in the US does involve subprocessors in the US. For EU customers we support EU-only processing regions and SCCs. If Helix requires EU-only handling for telemetry, we can propose an addendum for region-bound processing and include contractual Standard Contractual Clauses for transfers.

3) Logs & retention: by default request logs are retained for 90 days (configurable). We can produce aggregated telemetry (no identifiers) for long-term measurement needs.

Open items for Helix to confirm: 
- Do you need raw advertising identifiers (e.g., pub_cookie, ad_id) to be preserved in any downstream exports?
- Do any downstream ad partners require raw identifiers rather than tokens?

If you can confirm those two, Evelyn and I will produce a DPA redline with two options: token-only flow and token+raw (with additional contractual controls). I've attached our suggested DPA redline draft — DPA_v3_redlines.pdf.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Mark — following up with the proposed path:

1) Default recommendation: enable Tokenized mapping (hashed token per Helix account) and configure telemetry retention to 30/90/365 windows per dataset. This removes raw ad ids from Redwood logs and keeps measurement intact via tokens.

2) For any partner exports that require raw ids, we suggest adding a partner-level contract and scoping disclosure to named partners only. If Helix confirms a short list of partners we will add them to the subprocessor list and restrict flows.

3) Legal: Neha has supplied a redline (attached). If you approve token-only, legal can finalize an addendum that includes EU-region processing option and SCCs.
